title: How to clear browsing history in Safari on Mac: steps, options, and what stays behind
metaTitle: How to Clear Browsing History in Safari on Mac (2026)

intro: To clear browsing history in Safari on Mac, choose History > Clear History, click the pop-up menu, pick how far back to clear, then confirm. Clearing removes that history from your Mac and from your other Apple devices when Safari syncs through iCloud, but it leaves the separate histories that websites keep.
tldr: Choose History > Clear History in Safari's menu bar, then pick a time range from the pop-up.
Apple's pages do not list the time range options, so read the list on your screen before you click.
With iCloud set up for Safari, the clear also applies to your other Apple devices.
Downloaded files stay on disk. Only the downloads list is cleared.
No Apple page we checked gives a default keyboard shortcut for this command.

blocks.text: Clearing history in Safari takes only a moment. The part people miss is what the clear leaves behind. Clearing removes Safari's own list of pages. The sites you visited keep their own records, and your downloaded files stay on disk. Apple's guide treats these as separate things, so read the rest of this page before you assume everything is gone.
Clear Safari history on Mac, step by step

Start by making Safari the front app. The menu bar across the top of the screen should show Safari's own menus, including History. If it shows another app's menus, click an empty part of the Safari window first. Then open the History menu and choose Clear History.
Clicking Clear History opens a small window with a pop-up menu. Nothing is removed until you confirm. That gives you one last chance to change your mind, so use it.

blocks.title: Missing History menu?
blocks.text: The History menu only shows when Safari is the active app. Click the Safari window, then look at the menu bar again.

Use the pop-up menu to pick how far back Safari clears. Then click the Clear History button in that window to confirm. HowTo Geek describes this window as having a drop-down and a Clear History button, in a 2020 article about custom shortcuts. Apple's Mac page we checked does not name the button or the options, so read the screen as you go.
Safari history time ranges on Mac

Apple's Mac guide tells you to choose how far back to clear, but it does not list the choices. The list on your screen is the one that counts. The choices may differ between macOS releases, and we could not confirm the exact list on the newest version. Read it before you click.

Here is a worked example. You searched for a birthday gift earlier today, and you do not want that search in your history. Open the pop-up and pick the shortest range that still covers that search. Then confirm. Older visits stay in place, because a short range leaves them alone. Choosing all history would have removed them too.

Choose all history when you are handing a shared Mac to someone else or cleaning up a machine you no longer use. A clear removes everything inside the range you picked. Check the range one more time before you confirm.

Read the range as a question. Ask what the Mac should remember after the clear, not what you want to forget. That framing stops you from wiping research you still need when only one search needed to go.
What clearing Safari history removes and what it leaves behind

Apple's Mac guide is specific on this point. Clearing history removes it from all your Apple devices when iCloud is set up for Safari. It does not clear the browsing histories that websites keep on their own. Downloaded files stay where they are. Only the downloads list is cleared. The table below sums up the main cases.

rows: Removed for the range you picked
Safari history on other Apple devices
blocks.caption: What the Mac Clear History command reaches, based on Apple's Mac guide

blocks.text: The downloads row causes the most confusion. If you want a file gone, you still need to delete it yourself in Finder. The clear helps only with the list of what you downloaded.
Websites are the other half of the picture. Clearing Safari does not change what those sites hold. Apple's guide says so directly, so plan around it rather than hoping the clear reaches them.
Clear Safari history with iCloud sync on

If you sign in to Safari with the same Apple ID on your iPhone, iPad, and other Macs, the clear follows you. Apple says the history is removed from every device in that setup. Plan for this before you clear on a shared family account, since one clear reaches all of them.

Say you clear your Mac on a Sunday night to tidy up a gift search. The same clear also removes that history from your iPad and your other Mac, if they use the same Apple ID and iCloud for Safari. Tell the people on that account before you clear.

blocks.title: Sync can seem to block a clear
blocks.text: Some blog posts say iCloud sync can block the clear. We could not confirm that from any Apple page we opened. If a clear does not stick, check iCloud settings on each device first.
Clear cookies and website data separately

History and cookies are different things. Apple's iPhone and iPad page has a Clear History and Website Data option, with a timeframe. The Mac pages we opened describe clearing history only. They do not name a cookie option, so do not assume the History clear removes cookies.

To check cookies on your Mac, look in Safari's settings for website data controls. Apple's Mac pages we opened do not walk through that path. Use Safari's Help menu or the Safari User Guide to find the steps for your version.

If you are not sure whether a setting covers cookies, read the option names on the screen before you click. Apple's pages name the iPhone and iPad option, but the Mac pages we opened do not. Trust what you see in front of you more than what a blog post says.
Why so many people clear their browsing history

The habit is common. A 2013 Pew Research Center survey of 1,002 adults found that 64% clear cookies and their browser history. The same survey found that 41% had disabled cookies altogether. That survey is more than a decade old, so treat the numbers as a snapshot.

The same survey reports that 86% of internet users had taken steps to remove or mask their digital footprints. Clearing history is one of those steps. It does not hide your activity from your network or your internet provider. Know that limit before you rely on it.
Keyboard shortcuts for Clear History in Safari

None of the Apple pages we opened gives a default keyboard shortcut for Clear History. Several blog posts repeat Shift-Command-Delete. We could not verify that from a source we opened, so test it yourself before you rely on it.

HowTo Geek's 2020 article shows how to make your own shortcut for the Clear History menu item. It uses Shift+Command+H only as an example. Pick a combination no other app already uses. Test any custom shortcut with a harmless search first, so you know it clears only what you expect.
Why Clear History is greyed out

Apple's troubleshooting page names two causes for a greyed-out Clear History button. The first is that there is no data to clear. The second is that web content restrictions in Screen Time may be on. That page is written for iPhone and iPad, so treat these as likely causes on a Mac, not confirmed Mac behavior.

items: Open the History menu and check for recent items. An empty history has nothing to clear.
Check Screen Time for web content restrictions, which Apple says can grey out the button.
Quit Safari completely, open it again, and check the History menu before you try once more.
If the Mac belongs to a work or school account, ask the administrator before you change any limits.

blocks.text: Crash reports after clearing history on macOS Tahoe

A MacRumors forum post dated September 17, 2025 describes a user on macOS Tahoe 26.0, build 25A354. The user says every clear of history produced a crash report for Safari. The thread had no replies and no fix when we checked. One report does not prove a wide bug, but it is worth checking.

To see the report yourself, open Console and look for Safari under Crash Reports, as the forum post describes. Then update macOS and Safari through System Settings > General > Software Update. Clear history again to see whether the crash returns.
Mistakes people make when clearing Safari history

Most problems come from a few habits. People clear too much or too little, or they expect the clear to reach places it cannot reach. The list below covers the slips that Apple's pages and the forum post make easy to fall into.

items: Choosing all history when a short range was the goal.
Expecting a clear to delete downloaded files. Only the downloads list goes.
Forgetting that other Apple devices lose the same history when iCloud sync is on.
Assuming websites forget you. Their own records stay where they are.
Clearing before you bookmark a page you still need.

blocks.text: The first mistake costs the most time. People pick a broad range by accident, then search for the one thing they meant to delete. Read the range before you confirm, and check the History menu afterward. That habit takes seconds and saves the most trouble.
Check that the history is gone

After you confirm, open the History menu and look at the recent items. If the range you picked is empty, the clear worked on this Mac. If items remain, the range was probably shorter than you meant. Clear again with a longer range and check once more.

Remember what that check cannot show. It does not tell you about a site's own records, your downloaded files, or your network traffic. Those stay in place after the clear, so the check covers only Safari's own list.
Where to find the official steps and what to do next

The official source is Apple's Safari User Guide for macOS. It has a version selector that lists macOS 27 down to High Sierra. Pick the version that matches your Mac before you follow older steps, since menu names can change between releases.

If you clear history often, decide what you want to keep first. Clearing history is one of several things Safari stores, and it does not cover everything. Pick a routine you can actually keep, such as clearing at the end of each shared session, and stick to it.

When you finish, check the Downloads folder in Finder, decide whether any file should go, and confirm that the clear reached the devices you expected. Those three checks cover what the clear could not reach.

faq.question: Will clearing Safari history remove it from my iPhone too?
faq.answer: If iCloud is set up for Safari, Apple says the history is removed from all your Apple devices. If a device is not set up that way, it keeps its own history after you clear the Mac.

faq.question: Does clearing history remove the history that websites keep?
faq.answer: No. Apple says clearing history does not clear the browsing histories that websites keep independently. Clearing on your Mac does not reach those records, so the sites keep what they already hold.

faq.question: Will clearing history delete files I downloaded?
faq.answer: No. Apple says downloaded files are not removed. Only the downloads list is cleared. Delete the files in Finder yourself if you want them gone.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for Clear History in Safari on Mac?
faq.answer: None of the Apple pages we opened lists a default shortcut. Blog posts mention Shift-Command-Delete, but we could not verify it. HowTo Geek describes making your own shortcut for the menu item, which you can test with a harmless search first.

faq.question: Why is Clear History greyed out on my Mac?
faq.answer: Apple says the button is greyed out when there is no data to clear, or when web content restrictions in Screen Time may be on. Apple's page on this is written for iPhone and iPad, so check both causes on your Mac.

faq.question: Which macOS version do these steps match?
faq.answer: The steps match Apple's current Safari User Guide for macOS 27. We could not confirm the final Safari release number, so check the menu on your own Mac if anything looks different.

faq.question: Does clearing history hide my activity from my network or internet provider?
faq.answer: No. Clearing history only changes what Safari keeps on your Mac and on any devices that sync with it. Your network and internet provider can still see your traffic.

steps.name: Make Safari the active app
steps.text: Click any part of the Safari window so Safari is the front app. The menu bar then shows Safari's own menus, including History.
steps.tip: If you do not see History in the menu bar, Safari is not the active app.

steps.name: Choose History > Clear History
steps.text: In the menu bar, click History, then click Clear History. A small window opens with a pop-up menu. Nothing is removed yet.

steps.name: Pick how far back to clear
steps.text: Click the pop-up menu in the Clear History window and choose how far back Safari should clear. Read the list before you click, because Apple's Mac page does not name the options.
steps.tip: Choose the shortest range that covers what you want gone.

steps.name: Confirm the clear
steps.text: Click the Clear History button in that window. Safari removes the history for the range you picked.

steps.name: Check the History menu
steps.text: Open the History menu again and look at the recent items. If the range you picked is empty, the clear worked on this Mac.
steps.tip: Items still listed usually mean the range was shorter than you meant.

steps.name: Delete downloaded files if you need to
steps.text: The clear does not delete downloaded files. Open Finder and check your Downloads folder if you want those files gone too.

troubleshooting.fix: Check that the History menu has items to clear. Then check web content restrictions in Screen Time, which Apple says can block the button. Apple's page on this is written for iPhone and iPad, so Mac steps may differ.

troubleshooting.problem: The clear does not reach my other devices
troubleshooting.fix: Check that each device uses the same Apple ID with iCloud set up for Safari. Apple says the clear reaches every device in that setup. We could not confirm that some blog posts claim sync blocks clearing.

troubleshooting.problem: Safari makes a crash report after each clear
troubleshooting.fix: A macOS Tahoe 26.0 user reported this in 2025 with no fix. Check Console under Crash Reports for Safari, update macOS and Safari in System Settings, then test again.

troubleshooting.problem: History seems to come back after clearing
troubleshooting.fix: Other devices or the sites' own records may still hold it. Clearing on your Mac does not reach the history that websites keep independently.

troubleshooting.problem: Downloaded files are still on my Mac
troubleshooting.fix: Only the downloads list is cleared. Delete the files from Finder yourself.
